meaning:
μεθύω
(μέθυ, wine, cf. μέθη), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁכַר, רָוָה ;]
to be drunken: Mat.24:49, Jhn.2:10, Act.2:15, 1Co.11:21, 1Th.5:7; metaphorically, Rev.17:2, 6.†
(AS)

elsewhere.note: and begins to beat his fellow servants, and eat and drink with the drunkards,
and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk freely, then that which is worse. You have kept the good wine until now!”
For these aren’t drunken, as you suppose, seeing it is only the third hour of the day.
For in your eating each one takes his own supper first. One is hungry, and another is drunken.
For those who sleep, sleep in the night; and those who are drunk are drunk in the night.
I saw the woman drunken with the blood of the saints, and with the blood of the martyrs of Jesus. When I saw her, I wondered with great amazement.
